name: Des Moines
tagline: Insurance Capital with Farm-to-Table Charm and Midwestern Value
description: Des Moines is one of America's most underrated FIRE destinations, combining a remarkably low cost of living with a revitalized downtown, thriving farm-to-table dining scene, and an extensive network of bike trails. As the insurance capital of the country, the city has a stable economy and a growing cultural identity. The Des Moines Riverwalk, Pappajohn Sculpture Park, and a booming East Village neighborhood make this much more than just cornfields and cubicles.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: High – consistently ranked among safest mid-size US cities
quickFacts.climate: Continental with hot, humid summers and cold, snowy winters

housing.description: A modest 1BR in Beaverdale, Sherman Hill, or North of Grand, or a tidy studio near the East Village — safe, no frills

dining.description: Occasional casual meals out; most eating done at home

healthcare.description: A subsidized Silver plan on Iowa's ACA marketplace, assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600; above that, the full Iowa price runs about $705 or more. Priced for an early retiree aged 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with insurance, fuel, and upkeep — the practical baseline in a low-transit metro; summer trail-biking supplements but does not replace it

entertainment.description: A budget gym, a few streaming services, and the occasional ticket or night out

1M.lifestyle: Life here is grounded and quiet, built around a modest one-bedroom in an established neighborhood like Beaverdale or Sherman Hill. Cooking at home is the norm, with an occasional casual meal out, and a paid-off used car handles the errands that Des Moines's light transit cannot. Healthcare rests on a subsidized marketplace Silver plan, so keeping income under the ACA subsidy cutoff matters. It is a comfortable, unshowy baseline that still leaves room for a gym, streaming, and the city's long recreational trails.

housing.description: A well-kept 1BR in the East Village, Downtown, or a newer mid-market building with in-unit laundry and parking

dining.description: Regular meals out — neighborhood bistros and the odd nicer dinner — a few times a week

healthcare.description: A mid-grade Silver plan near the benchmark as income approaches the subsidy cliff and credits thin out

transportation.description: A newer, more reliable vehicle with insurance and fuel

entertainment.description: A full-service gym, live events, and hobby or recreation spending

2M.lifestyle: This tier trades up to a newer one-bedroom in the East Village or Downtown and loosens the budget across the board. Dining out becomes a regular pleasure rather than a treat, groceries lean fresher and higher-quality, and a more reliable car replaces the bare-bones commuter. Healthcare shifts toward a mid-grade Silver plan as subsidies thin. The result is easy, unpinched everyday living with real discretionary margin.

housing.description: A premium 1BR (or compact 2BR) in a luxury building such as LEVEL in the East Village or a Downtown high-rise, with full amenities

dining.description: Frequent restaurant dining including upscale spots, with wine and the occasional tasting menu

healthcare.description: A full-price Silver plan, since income at this budget sits above the subsidy cutoff. At age 50 the benchmark Silver runs about $700 a month and the cheapest about $640, so $680 is a realistic middle.

transportation.description: A reliable late-model car, fully insured, with fuel and maintenance, plus occasional rideshare

entertainment.description: A premium fitness club, cultural events, hobbies, and light travel

3M.lifestyle: Full financial independence looks like a premium apartment in a full-amenity building, frequent upscale dinners, and organic, specialty groceries. Healthcare is now a full-price unsubsidized Silver plan, reflecting income above the subsidy cutoff. Transportation is a late-model car with rideshare on tap, and there is steady spending on a premium gym, culture, and light travel. It is a polished, self-directed lifestyle with no routine trade-offs.

housing.description: A top-floor luxury rental in the metro's best buildings, or a high-end leased single-family home in West Des Moines / the Waterbury area — near the ceiling of the local rental market (verified: luxury-apt avg ~$1,636, so $2,200 is top-of-band; trimmed from $2,400)

dining.description: Frequent fine dining at the metro's best tables (e.g., Proudfoot & Bird) with wine and entertaining

healthcare.description: A full-price unsubsidized low-deductible Gold plan with generous out-of-pocket headroom

transportation.description: A near-new or leased premium vehicle, fully insured, with fuel, maintenance, and rideshare on demand

entertainment.description: Premium club membership, cultural patronage, recreation, and regular getaways

domesticHelp.description: Biweekly professional housekeeping at local rates (~$140/visit)

luxuryExtras.description: Discretionary lifestyle: club dues, seasonal travel, fine wine, and premium services

5M.lifestyle: At this level the home is a top-floor luxury rental or a high-end leased house at the edge of what Des Moines offers, and the calendar fills with fine dining and entertaining. A low-deductible Gold plan removes healthcare friction, a near-new premium car sits in the garage, and biweekly housekeeping frees up time. Discretionary spending — club dues, seasonal travel, fine wine — becomes a standing line rather than an occasional splurge. This is affluent living with staff support and generous slack.

housing.description: The very top of the local rental market — a premium penthouse or high-end executive leased home in West Des Moines, Waterbury, or Glen Oaks (rental stock at this level is genuinely thin — see confidence)

dining.description: Fine dining as routine, chef's tables, private events, and top wine

healthcare.description: A top unsubsidized domestic plan paired with concierge/direct-primary-care — a full-service US arrangement, not an expat plan

transportation.description: A luxury vehicle (owned or leased) with full insurance, fuel, maintenance, plus on-demand car service

entertainment.description: Premium club and cultural patronage, frequent travel, and well-funded hobbies

domesticHelp.description: Weekly housekeeping plus periodic deep-clean and additional household help

luxuryExtras.description: Country-club dues, seasonal travel, fine wine and art, personal services, and a big-ticket discretionary buffer

10M.lifestyle: The top tier commands the ceiling of the local market: a premium penthouse or executive home, fine dining as routine, and concierge-level healthcare layered onto a top domestic plan. A luxury vehicle and on-demand car service handle mobility, weekly household help keeps everything effortless, and a large discretionary buffer covers country-club life, travel, and big-ticket wants. Everything is optimized for ease and status within a metro whose costs stay modest even at the summit.
